A bowl contains 1 candy and 5 cockroaches. Each drawn cockroach is put back in the bowl before the next draw. Let X be the draw on which the candy is first picked. Find p(2)=P(X=2).
Hints: Cockroach first, replace it, then candy;Because of replacement the bowl always has 6 objects

Question Choices: A bowl contains 1 candy and 5 cockroaches. Each drawn cockroach is put back in the bowl before the next draw. Let X be the draw on which the candy is first picked. Which value of k has the largest probability p(k)?
Hints: Compare p(1), p(2), p(3), ...;Each p(k) is 5/6 of the one before it
Solution: $p(k)=\left(\frac{5}{6}\right)^{k-1}\frac{1}{6}$ shrinks by a factor of $\frac{5}{6}$ each time $k$ increases by $1$.;So the largest value is $p(1)=\frac{1}{6}$, and the most likely draw for the candy is $k=1$.
